title: Component taxonomy as canonical source of truth
description:
Define the component taxonomy as the single source of truth for detector subtypes and corpus annotations. Annotators pick from a defined list; no inventing subtypes.

Feature: Component taxonomy governs detector and annotation subtypes
Scenario: Detector emits a subtype not in the taxonomy
  Given a scanner detector that would emit a component subtype
  When the subtype is not declared in component-taxonomy.yaml
  Then the detector must add the subtype to the taxonomy first
  And no ad-hoc subtype is emitted
Scenario: Annotator labels a component
  Given a corpus repo with a component detection
  When the annotator assigns a subtype
  Then the subtype must exist in component-taxonomy.yaml

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Reparenting off closed epic KDATAP-d0db51. Still a live product question; overlaps KDATAP-08a0ac (component/flow identity policy). Taxonomy YAML as annotator constraint remains this story.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## Reparented here, and it is the answer to half of KDATAP-08a0ac — but the scenarios only cover one direction

Measured the corpus against `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`: of 563 component annotations, **481 (85%) use a key whose rest is a literal taxonomy subtype id** — `asset:database` x182, `asset:api` x118, `asset:auth_service` x110, `asset:service` x41, `asset:cache` x14, `asset:config` x8, `actor:customer`, `actor:admin`. Gold labels are the same vocabulary. So the second scenario here ("annotator labels a component ... the subtype must exist in component-taxonomy.yaml") is already satisfied in practice — the annotation agents adopted the taxonomy the day it landed (Aug 30, `4ca34cd`; 560 of 563 component annotations authored the same day).

The first scenario is the one with a gap, and it is wider than the Gherkin says.

**Nothing in `src/` reads `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`.** The only consumer in the repo is `tests/unit/taxonomy.spec.ts`, which checks that subtypes appearing in the three classifier YAMLs are declared in the taxonomy. That enforces "no ad-hoc subtype" reasonably well, but it is a test-time containment check, not runtime governance — and crucially it says nothing about the identity the engine actually emits.

`componentIdentity()` emits `${type}:${name.toLowerCase()}` — `asset:pg`, `asset:psycopg2`, `asset:django orm`. The subtype the taxonomy governs never appears in the key the scorer compares. So the taxonomy governs a field that eval ignores, while eval scores a field the taxonomy has no opinion about. That is why component recall reads ~0 on packets with 0 unread.

### Suggested extension to this story

Add a third scenario covering the direction that is missing — the identity, not just the subtype:

```gherkin
Feature: Component taxonomy governs detector and annotation subtypes
Scenario: Component identity used for evaluation comes from the taxonomy
  Given a scanner detector emits a component
  When the evaluation harness computes that component's subject key
  Then the key is "<type>:<subType>" using taxonomy ids
  And a component with no subType is reported as a taxonomy gap, not scored as a match
```

Two things that scenario forces into the open, both of which KDATAP-08a0ac needs answered anyway:

1. `DetectedComponent.subType` is **optional** (`subType?: string`), and `decideComponentTypeAndSubType` has paths that leave it undefined. Subtype coverage on a real corpus run has to be measured before `type:subType` can be an identity — otherwise 85% of gold starts matching `asset:undefined`.
2. `actor:user` (30 gold cases) is not a declared subtype, though `customer` and `admin` are. `application-injection.ts` already injects a user actor via `getInjectedUserActorSubtype`, so the engine has an opinion the taxonomy does not record. Either add `user` to the taxonomy or fix the gold.

Also one gold bug found while counting: a single component annotation carries the label `third_party`, which is a *type*, not a subtype — exactly what scenario 2 is meant to prevent, so it is a live counterexample worth keeping.

### Scope note

This story answers the **component** half of KDATAP-08a0ac. It does not reach data-flows: 436 flow annotations use 424 distinct bare-endpoint keys (`flow:password->wp_check_password`, `flow:session->cookie`) that are neither taxonomy subtypes nor vendor names. That half needs its own decision.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Superseded in part by the KDATAP-08a0ac decision — and the scenario I proposed above needs amending

My earlier comment recommended eval component identity become `${type}:${subType}`. The decision on KDATAP-08a0ac supersedes that with structured canonical fields — type, taxonomy subtype, instance/vendor when known, evidence — and that is the better answer: it grades vendor resolution as its own dimension instead of collapsing it out of the key, which is what a derived `type:subType` string would have done.

What survives from this story unchanged, and is now confirmed by the decision: **the component taxonomy is authoritative for type and subtype.** Measured, 481 of 563 component gold keys (85%) already use a literal `component-taxonomy.yaml` subtype id, so scenario 2 here holds in practice.

The gap in scenario 1 also stands, and is wider than the Gherkin states. Nothing in `src/` reads `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`; the only consumer is `tests/unit/taxonomy.spec.ts`, which checks that subtypes used by the three classifier YAMLs are declared in the taxonomy. That is test-time containment, and it says nothing about the identity the scorer compares.

### Amended scenario

Replacing the third scenario I proposed above — it asserted a `type:subType` key, which the decision has now ruled against:

```gherkin
Feature: Component taxonomy governs detector and annotation subtypes
Scenario: Evaluation identity fields come from the taxonomy
  Given a scanner detector emits a component
  When the evaluation harness builds that component's canonical expectation
  Then type and subtype are taxonomy ids
  And instance is required only where gold asserts a vendor
  And a component with no subtype is reported as a taxonomy gap rather than a match
```

The middle assertion is the one that matters most, and the reason is on KDATAP-08a0ac: all 473 asset annotations carry a `subject.name` that is a code-level instance (`directus_users`, `LocalAuthDriver`, `UsersService`). If a migration reads those as the canonical instance field, "strict all-required-fields" would require an instance for 85% of component gold and the strict result stays near zero — the exact outcome the decision is meant to avoid.

### Blockers this story should carry

- **`actor:user`, 30 gold cases, is not a declared subtype** while `customer` and `admin` are. Under "the taxonomy is authoritative", these cannot be migrated until the taxonomy declares `user`. `src/classifier/application-injection.ts` already injects a user actor via `getInjectedUserActorSubtype`, so the engine holds an opinion the taxonomy does not record.
- **One gold component label is `third_party`** — a type, not a subtype. Single instance, and a live counterexample for exactly the rule scenario 2 asserts.

### Scope

This story covers the component half. It does not reach data flows: 436 annotations, 424 distinct bare-endpoint keys, no taxonomy subtypes and no vendors. KDATAP-08a0ac carries that as a separate regold.

comments.author: rap@endymion.com
comments.text: Remaining actionable work from this story is already filed: KDATAP-ea44fe (`user` subtype) and KDATAP-4b0df4 (`third_party` label). The structured-identity half is superseded by the KDATAP-08a0ac decision and is implemented on KDATAP-2e8f9f / KDATAP-1076a9 after the gate rulings. Leaving this story open until those two gold/taxonomy defects are done.
